text:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Canary rollout (model=v4.0.1) causing p99 latency spike on /v1/stream endpoints. p99 jumped from 280ms -> 2.3s over last 10m, p95 degraded to ~650ms. SLO (p99<1s) breached. Auto-fallback did not trigger for streaming requests. Paging oncall.

jordan: acknowledged. I'm oncall and will dig in now. Which canary percentage is live?

priya: canary at 10% across us-east-1, us-west-2. Traffic shift started ~1849123300. Metrics: token throughput up ~18%, tail latency across seq>1024 spiked.

ken: seeing streaming stalls in logs, repeated `write()` hangs from runtime for some requests. KV cache miss rate increased at the same time. Might be cache pressure from v4's longer context usage.

anya: customer-ops flagged two paying customers reporting UI stalls (chat widgets freezing). They see partial streaming then long gap then full blob. Correlates with p99 spikes.

jordan: good context. Triage plan: 1) Immediate mitigation: shift canary back to 0% (traffic-split) or rollback v4 to v3 for canary group. 2) Investigate root cause (KV cache, kernel selection, quantization path). 3) Notify customers and status page.

priya: trying traffic-shift now. Running routing update: ```
redwoodctl traffic update --route "/v1/stream" --from model:v4.0.1@canary=10% --to model:v3.9.8=10% --set-canary=0%
```

ops-bot: action taken: traffic-shift job submitted (job id jid-1934).

ken: I see job succeeded, route config updated, canary removed at 1849123412. But p99 still elevated for ~2 minutes, likely in-flight sessions draining.

jordan: rolling back canary variant explicit call: ```
POST /admin/rollbacks
{
  "route":"/v1/stream",
  "from":"v4.0.1",
  "to":"v3.9.8",
  "drain_seconds":120
}
```

ops-bot: rollback triggered by jordan (audit id ar-8843).

priya: monitoring metrics — p99 trending down: 2.3s -> 1.1s within 60s, p95 down to 420ms. Streaming stalls count decreased but still seeing occasional spikes.

ken: pulling runtime logs from a host with high tail latency: ```
[2024-11-29T12:34:22Z] model=v4.0.1 worker=nv-23 seq_len=2048 kv_cache_misses=0.48 backend_write_ms=1320
[2024-11-29T12:34:22Z] stream-session id=abc123 stalled for 1500ms waiting on write()
```

anya: flagged customers informed: "We observed elevated latency impacting streaming responses during a canary rollout. We rolled back the canary and are continuing to monitor; will follow up with root cause." Customer-ops requested ETA for permanent fix.

jordan: notes from quick root-cause guess: v4 increases attention key sizes due to longer context usage; kernel selection chooses a different matmul path that regresses tail under high concurrency. Also higher memory working set causing more KV cache churn. Need logs from kernel selector and profiling.

ken: starting collection: enabling debug trace for kernel-selection on a small subset (logs saved to s3://rw-infra/artifacts/1849123456/kernel-traces). Also capturing perf counters and NV profiler snapshot for one affected host.

priya: also enabling prefix caching knob for streaming router to see if early hits prevent stalls: ```
redwoodctl router set /v1/stream --prefix-kv-cache=on --cache-ttl=300
```

ops-bot: prefix-kv-cache enable job queued (jid-1935).

jordan: operational mitigation checklist: - rollback complete - drain period honored - enable prefix cache - rate-limit new streaming sessions to 50rps for canary pool until we have kernel trace. Apply temporary circuit-breaker for sequences > 1024 to force sync generation path.

ken: implementing circuit breaker rule: ```
redwoodctl policy create --name tail-protect --route /v1/stream --if "seq_len>1024" --then "limit=1,mode=sync,fallback=model:v3.9.8"
```

priya: policy applied. Monitoring shows spike count almost gone. p99 back under 900ms at 1849123540. :thumbsup:

anya: preparing incident summary for customers: short timeline, impact, mitigation, next steps. Will post to status.redwood.ai/incidents/1849123456 and ping Customer Success.

jordan: moving to postmortem cadence. Assign owners: RCA infra/eng-runtime (ken), model-team (priya) to look at v4 memory/kernel changes, devex (anya) for runbook updates and canary-sizing guidance.

ops-bot: incident ticker opened: INC-2024-872, severity S2 (customer-facing but mitigated).

ken: early traces show kernel selection hit matmul-path idx 7 (non-fused) for some kv sizes; fallback path (idx 3) is faster for large batch/seq combos. Suspect selection heuristic needs update for seq>1024.

priya: model-team will reproduce on bench with seq=2048 and concurrent=32, then test kernel option matrix. If confirmed, we can release a fix to kernel selector and ship a patched v4.0.2 or adjust heuristics at serving layer.

anya: handoff: jordan -> sre-oncall taking next 2 hours. Handoff notes: rollback done, prefix cache on, tail-protect policy active, traces uploaded, customers notified, INC-2024-872 open.

sre-oncall: ack. I'll keep monitoring for the next 2 hours and escalate if p99 creeps back above 1s.

jordan: thanks everyone. Follow-ups: - ken/priya to post RCA in /doc/incidents within 72h - anya to update canary runbook with explicit prefix-caching and seq-limits - ops to add automated health-check that validates p99 under canary before scaling canary past 5%.

customer-ops: noted, will follow up with affected accounts with the timeline and engineering next steps.

ops-bot: incident auto-close check scheduled in 6h. Keep thread updated with new findings. :white_check_mark:
